x: …two very fine efforts, John finishing second to Gordon Pirie in the 1500 metres with a time of 3m.59 1s. and Pat chased John Disley home in the 3 miles to finish less than two seconds behind in 14m.39 6s. and incidently beat Langridge of S.L.H. who is no mean performer.…

The Sunday Telegraph suggests that a strong candidate is John Disley and quote no less a sponsorship than the International Athletes"Club" and in particular Peter Hildreth, Chris Brasher and Derek Johnson.

The second day's programme produced a record equalling run in the domestic 220 by McDonald Bailey in 21.2, a good 440 yds win by Olympic Champion Arthur Wint in 48.1 and the first of many wins by John Disley in the 2 mile steeplechase.
Horace Ashenfelter of America drew away from Kazantsev of the USSR, who just prevailed over our own John Disley; the Olympic Record was improved by six seconds.
